svg.title: A miscibility gap: where one composition costs more than two
svg.desc: Left: a sketch of the Gibbs energy of a symmetric regular solid solution with an interaction above the threshold of 2 RT: the curve has two wells, a hump between its inflection points (the spinodal), and the common tangent touches it at two compositions. Right: a composition inside the gap is cheaper as the two compositions of the tangent, in the proportions of the lever rule; the phase is declared twice, one instance on each.
